Source 22806/801B12970 made 15 transfers in the alert window with repetitive small amounts consistent with structuring.

Source 25536/80313A000 sent identical large amounts twice, four days apart.
Destination 121415/80BA7C7B0 received exactly €4,281.39 six times over the window.

findings.narrative: Account 10709/80692A790 acted as a hub receiving funds from 4 source accounts and sending to 3 destination accounts over an 8-day window. All 4 sources (25536/80313A000, 22806/801B12970, 111121/80C2C7140, 17222/8041EDC70) have zero other counterparties and only send to this hub. All 3 destinations (225690/80FFF9840, 121415/80BA7C7B0, 18819/805B9B260) have zero other counterparties and only receive from this hub. The hub itself was active for only 10 days (first seen Sep 1, last seen Sep 10). Source 80313A000 sent identical large amounts twice (€5,832.55 and €25,861.50 on Sep 2 and Sep 9). Source 801B12970 made 15 transfers in the window with repetitive small amounts (€801.99, €204.14, €201.95) consistent with structuring. Destination 80BA7C7B0 received exactly €4,281.39 six times. The pattern, short account lifespans, lack of other business relationships, and repetitive amounts indicate a gather-scatter laundering scheme rather than legitimate activity.
